customManagers.description: dsh has no published container image, so stacks/dsh builds from upstream's npm package with the version pinned in compose.yaml's build.args (see that file for why it lives there and not in the Dockerfile). The docker-compose manager only reads `image:` keys, so the build arg needs its own manager.

packageRules.description: Topic Docker image PRs by the bare image name (Renovate's default prepends a 'dependency ' noun).

dsh is a developer preview that has only ever published prereleases (0.0.1-rc.N, then 0.1.x-rc.N, now 0.1.2-alpha.N). With the default ignoreUnstable, Renovate allows a prerelease upgrade only when major.minor.patch match the current one — rc.7 -> rc.8 would be offered, but a move to a new prerelease line would be dropped with no PR and no dashboard entry. Upstream has already made that jump twice (0.0.1-rc.5 -> 0.1.0-rc.2 and 0.1.1-rc.2 -> 0.1.2-alpha.1), so opt into unstable explicitly. Note that npm's `latest` dist-tag still points at the older rc line while `alpha` carries the newer one; Renovate ranks by version, not dist-tag, so the alpha is still offered. Breaking changes are expected: read the release notes before merging.
Mastodon ships its web/sidekiq image and the streaming image in lockstep at the same version, so group their updates into one PR.

LinuxServer.io tags embed a build hash and -lsNN rebuild counter (1.43.2.10687-563d026ea-ls311); default docker versioning treats that suffix as a compatibility variant that must match exactly, so updates are never offered. Parse the tag explicitly instead.
Same LinuxServer.io problem for emby, whose tags look like 4.9.5.0-ls283 (no build hash).
Same LinuxServer.io problem for kometa, whose tags look like v2.4.4-ls103.
